qs.q: An infant requires temporary CSF diversion for intraventricular haemorrhage and ventriculitis, but definitive shunt placement is delayed because the CSF has high protein content. Why is high protein problematic for a shunt?
o: It causes immediate distal bowel perforation
It degrades the silicone tubing material
It would block a shunt valve
qs.e: High protein in the CSF would block a shunt valve, which is why an external ventricular drain is used until the CSF is clear. It does not directly degrade the silicone tubing or cause bowel perforation.

qs.q: A patient with communicating hydrocephalus and idiopathic intracranial hypertension cannot use the peritoneal cavity for CSF diversion due to previous abdominal surgeries. Which alternative permanent shunt can be utilized?
qs.e: Lumboperitoneal shunts are indicated for communicating hydrocephalus and idiopathic intracranial hypertension when the abdomen cannot be accessed. Ventriculogastric shunts are not standard physiological pathways used in neurosurgery.
qs.s: Hydrocephalus: Causes, Presentation and CSF Diversion (Shunts): MCQs

qs.q: A surgeon is planning CSF diversion for a patient with obstructive hydrocephalus secondary to a posterior fossa tumour. Which procedure can be performed before or during surgery as an alternative to an external ventricular drain?
qs.e: An endoscopic third ventriculostomy (ETV) or an external ventricular drain can be performed before or during surgery for CSF diversion. A lumboperitoneal shunt is contraindicated in obstructive hydrocephalus due to risk of herniation.
